stories.headline: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a Public Benefit Fund; Musk pledges SpaceX shares to US kids

key_facts.fact: On Oct 18, Anthropic said it will commit 5% of its shares to the new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to stockholder approval, with an extra 2% at the board's discretion for every 50% rise in value above a set baseline.
key_facts.excerpt: Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic's shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board's discretion for every 50% increase in the company's value above a set baseline.

key_facts.fact: The fund is a wholly owned LLC rather than a 501(c)(3), and none of its Anthropic equity will be used for lobbying or political giving; possible uses include large donations to nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations, e.g. for labor-market impacts.
key_facts.excerpt: We're establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3)... None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving... we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.

key_facts.fact: Combined with co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and an employee donation-match program used by about half of staff, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good.
key_facts.excerpt: When combined with today's announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing AI's labor-market impacts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue

key_facts.fact: At an IPO valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, the 5% stake would be worth $75 billion to $100 billion, Reuters calculated.
key_facts.excerpt: That would value a 5% stake toward the fund in a range of $75 billion to $100 billion.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk replied that he recommended giving shares directly to the public and pledged: 'Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.'
key_facts.excerpt: Musk said: "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many."

key_facts.fact: The announcement comes as Anthropic prepares an IPO that could start formal marketing as soon as the week of Nov. 9.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic... may start formally marketing its ... as soon as the week of Nov. 9

stories.headline: One hacker's AI agents broke into 100+ company sites, incl. Deere and SharkNinja, for ~$5,000

key_facts.fact: A Chinese-speaking hacker broke into websites of more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, outsourcing the work almost entirely to autonomous AI agents, according to NorForge researcher Snorre Fagerland, Reuters reported Oct 19.
key_facts.excerpt: a Chinese-speaking hacker broke into websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm equipment maker Deere, home appliance company SharkNinja and engine manufacturer Cummins. Yet the hacker did almost none of the work.

key_facts.fact: The agents had attempted to break into more than 1,200 sites; successful intrusions typically took about 23 hours, and instructions were under 100 Chinese characters.
key_facts.excerpt: As of late last week, their agents had attempted to break into more than 1,200 sites. Successful intrusions typically took around 23 hours

key_facts.fact: The campaign appeared to use a mix of DeepSeek and Anthropic's Claude Code and consumed roughly $5,000 in tokens, about $50 per successful hack.
key_facts.excerpt: appeared to be using a mixture of China's DeepSeek and Anthropic's Claude Code, had chewed up roughly $5,000 worth of tokens, or about $50 per successful hack.

key_facts.fact: Fagerland found about two dozen exposed instances of Cairn, an open-source AI problem-solving platform, being used for malicious activity starting around Oct 2; another hacker stole credit card data and one tried to rob a crypto exchange.
key_facts.excerpt: Beginning around October 2, Fagerland said he found about two dozen instances of Cairn being used for malicious activity... One of the hackers that Fagerland observed stole a trove of credit card data. Another tried to get AI agents to rob a cryptocurrency exchange.

key_facts.fact: Deere said there was no indication sensitive information was accessed; SharkNinja said a standalone product-support site was hit and the threat contained; Cummins said it was investigating a third-party vendor site.
key_facts.excerpt: a John Deere spokesperson said there is "no indication that sensitive information was accessed"... SharkNinja says the breach impacted a standalone site with product support information

key_facts.fact: Cairn's creator, @le1xia0, said the platform 'was never a hacking tool' and that misuse is a human decision.
key_facts.excerpt: Cairn's creator, who goes by @le1xia0, said earlier this month that the platform "was never a 'hacking tool,'"

stories.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017 open weights and opens Search and Fetch APIs to all developers

key_facts.fact: On Oct 17, DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on its website, app and API, calling it a 'Pareto improvement' in performance and cost.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek on Saturday released an updated version of its AI model... described the update as a "Pareto improvement" in performance and cost

key_facts.fact: The model scored 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1, up from 74.2, and 60.5 on Automation-Bench, up from 54.8; it was trained with reinforcement learning with self-feedback.
key_facts.excerpt: scored 77.0 on the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, up from 74.2 for its previous version, and 60.5 on Automation-Bench V1.0.6, compared with 54.8 previously

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek opened Search and Fetch APIs powered by its in-house search engine at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek also opened its Search and Fetch APIs to all users... Each Search or Fetch API endpoint costs $0.75 per 1,000 calls

key_facts.fact: Weights were published on Hugging Face and ModelScope; DeepSeek's cost chart puts a DeepSWE task at just under $0.20, versus about $0.50 for the previous Flash, though Opus 5 still leads on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Humanity's Last Exam.
key_facts.excerpt: published open weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope... DeepSeek's cost chart puts a DeepSWE task at just under $0.20, versus about $0.50 for the previous Flash

key_facts.fact: Vals AI ranked the new DeepSeek V4.1 as the #1 open-weight model on the Vals Index at $0.64 per task.
key_facts.excerpt: Deepseek v4.1 (10/17) is the new #1 open-weight model on the Vals Index. It is also cheap at just $0.64 / task.

stories.headline: Reflection releases Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0

key_facts.fact: On Oct 16, US lab Reflection released the weights of Beam, its first open-weight model, on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license, with a safety technical report.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we have released Beam's model weights on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license... the Beam Safety Technical Report shares the model's complete safety methodology and evaluations.

key_facts.fact: Beam is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501B total and 23B active parameters, a 1M-token context and five reasoning levels, aimed at coding and agentic use.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a mixture-of-experts (MoEs) model with 501B parameters (23B active per token), supports text as input, has a context window of 1M tokens, and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

key_facts.fact: Reflection pretrained Beam on 23.8 trillion tokens and ran RL with over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K Nvidia GB300 GPUs over four weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: We pretrained the model on 23.8 trillion diverse, curated, high-quality tokens... Our high-compute RL run generated over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs over 4 weeks of training.

key_facts.fact: Beam launched with 40+ partners, available on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, Together AI, Fireworks, OpenRouter, Ollama and others.
key_facts.excerpt: we're launching with an ecosystem of over 40 partners and integrations... Amazon Web Services... Google Cloud... Microsoft Foundry... Ollama... OpenRouter... Together AI

key_facts.fact: Beam ships with its own open-source Rust-based coding harness.
key_facts.excerpt: Beam ships with its own dedicated open source Rust based harness that delivers the best performance from the model.

stories.headline: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours with no human help

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind said four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours, operating only through code and text, writing 2,783 programs and coordinating via chat.
key_facts.excerpt: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours. Operating in a sandbox using only code and text, they wrote 2,783 programs, divided up jobs over chat, shared notes, and debugged errors together - all with no human help

key_facts.fact: The agents were dropped into a randomly generated world without assigned roles, strategies or game-specific tools and slew the Ender Dragon after 27 hours and 14 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: The Google Deepmind team dropped the agents into a randomly generated world without assigning roles, strategies, or game-specific tools... Over 27 hours and 14 minutes

key_facts.fact: Over the run the agents exchanged 229 chat messages, died 605 times and logged mistakes in a shared memory.
key_facts.excerpt: the four agents wrote a total of 2,783 JavaScript programs, exchanged 229 chat messages, and died 605 times.

key_facts.fact: The full session cost $1,620 at Gemini 4 Argon's standard price that takes effect in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The entire session cost $1,620 at the standard Gemini 4 Argon price that takes effect in 2027.

stories.headline: Anthropic: Claude Mythos 5 designed quantum circuits beating the best published ones

key_facts.fact: On Oct 16, Anthropic reported that Claude Mythos 5, given plain-language specs for eight quantum circuits and an automated evaluator, found designs improving on the best published circuits, sometimes by an order of magnitude or more.
key_facts.excerpt: Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.

key_facts.fact: The tasks spanned chemistry, optimization, physics simulation and number theory; Claude worked in a closed loop with no human input between rounds.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Mythos 5 could successfully work in a closed loop, proposing a circuit design, receiving feedback and a score from the evaluator program... with no human input between rounds

key_facts.fact: On the elliptic-curve point-addition task Claude worked for 53 hours with minimal human input and found a new approach to modular inversion; a separate result made the costliest step of a leading quantum optimization algorithm about 12x cheaper.
key_facts.excerpt: After working for 53 hours with minimal human input... Claude arrived at a completely new approach to the problem... The second makes the costliest step of a leading quantum optimization algorithm about 12x cheaper.

key_facts.fact: The headline elliptic-curve result was a 17-fold reduction in gate count at the cost of 12% more qubits; on seven of eight tasks it cut both qubits and Toffoli gates.
key_facts.excerpt: The headline result is a 17-fold reduction in gate count on an elliptic-curve circuit, at the cost of 12% more qubits.

key_facts.fact: The work was led by Andi Gu of Anthropic's STEM Fellows Program with Harvard's Susanne Yelin and Mikhail Lukin, co-founder of QuEra Computing.
key_facts.excerpt: The research team included Andi Gu, of Anthropic's STEM Fellows Program and Harvard; Alek H. Kemeny, of Anthropic and Susanne F. Yelin and Mikhail D. Lukin... Lukin is also co-founder and Chief Scientist of QuEra Computing.

stories.headline: Anthropic embeds six METR evaluators with 'employee-like' access and no veto on publication

key_facts.fact: On Oct 15, Anthropic said it has begun giving employee-like access to a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models, and METR will publish its risk assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing that we've started to give employee-like access to a team from METR... METR will publish the results of its risk assessments.

key_facts.fact: Six METR employees received company hardware, office space and internal-tool access roughly on par with Anthropic's own risk teams; Anthropic cannot veto publication but can require narrow redactions.
key_facts.excerpt: We've onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space, and access to internal tools and systems that are roughly on par with what our own risk assessment teams have access to... Anthropic can't veto publication

key_facts.fact: Anthropic set up three access tiers: SecureBio is in tier one reviewing the chem-bio chapter of its August Risk Report, METR is tier three; it is also working with Accenture and Faculty and in early talks with Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: SecureBio is currently in the first tier... The third tier is the arrangement we've described with METR... in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is not funding METR's work, CNBC reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is not funding METR's work, according to the company.

key_facts.fact: METR does not accept donations from AI companies or their staff and is funded by individuals, philanthropies and bodies such as the UK AI Security Institute.
key_facts.excerpt: The research group does not accept donations from AI companies or their staff. It is funded by donations from individuals and philanthropic organisations, as well as government bodies such as the UK's AI Security Institute.
